rationale: Contract C2 quota-classification table, ext2/ext3/ext4 row 'any of quota,usrquota,grpquota,prjquota,usrjquota,grpjquota | enabled | unknown | ext_quota_option' (contract.md:118). Derived from contract.md (frozen at lane commit 4dc80c1be48308075e83af17f15fbfe7e95e6cb8) and the named kernel sources only; no implementation was read (neither .ufo/waves/round-23/build/ImplQuota/ nor .scratch/round23/ImplQuota, and no sibling case file was used to derive the expectation). (1) Mount resolution: the probed path is /srv/journal/data with realpath /srv/journal/data. Contract C2 'Mount resolution' (contract.md:95-104) admits a mount whose mount point equals the realpath, is '/', or is followed by '/' in the realpath; the fixture's btrfs root line ('/') and its ext4 line ('/srv/journal') are therefore both candidates, and the longest mount point wins, so the chosen mount is '/srv/journal' with fstype 'ext4'. Field layout per proc.rst section 3.5 (S082): six fixed fields, then optional fields until the '-' separator, then filesystem type, mount source and super options as the last field (proc.rst:1970-1983; 'Parsers should ignore all unrecognised optional fields', proc.rst:1985) - so the ext4 line's super options are 'rw,user_xattr,acl,jqfmt=vfsv0,usrjquota=aquota.user' even though the line also carries the optional field 'shared:7'. (2) Device check: the chosen fstype is ext4 (not btrfs), and the mountinfo major:minor '8:2' equals the path's st_dev '8:2', so the contract's 'unknown / device_mismatch' branch is not taken; proc.rst:1975 defines field (3) major:minor as the 'value of st_dev for files on filesystem' (S082), so equality is the ordinary case for ext4 and the btrfs per-subvolume exemption (S081) is irrelevant here. (3) Classification: contract.md:105 parses the super options as a comma-split list whose key is the text before '=', giving keys rw, user_xattr, acl, jqfmt, usrjquota. 'usrjquota' is one of the contract's ext4 quota keys (quota, usrquota, grpquota, prjquota, usrjquota, grpjquota), so the enabled row applies: quota_state 'enabled', enforcement 'unknown' (this row's enforcement token; the ext4 filesystem itself ignores these options, which are used only by quota tools - ext4.rst:261-265 'These options are ignored by the filesystem', S083), basis 'ext_quota_option'. 'jqfmt' is not a member of the contract's ext4 key list, but the row is an 'any of' test, so jqfmt neither adds nor removes the verdict. (4) Verdict precedence: exactly one path is probed, it is enabled, and none is unknown, so exit 1 with finding_id QUOTA_ENABLED (contract.md:132-135); QUOTA_ENABLED is a runway-reporting finding, not a failure claim. (5) File-name non-disclosure: 'usrjquota=aquota.user' carries a quota file name in the option value (ext4.rst:267 'jqfmt=<quota type>, usrjquota=<file>, grpjquota=<file>', S083). The contract requires the probe to expose option keys only and never file names from option values (contract.md:124-130), so 'aquota.user' must not appear in the output; note that the sealed per-path comparison tuple for this case (path, fstype, mount_point, quota_state, enforcement, basis) cannot by itself detect such a leak, so that property needs an independent check - see the report for the ambiguity list and this coverage gap. Fixture realism: 'vfsv0' is the kernel's journal-quota format token (fs/ext4/super.c ext4_param_jqfmt maps 'vfsv0' to QFMT_VFS_V0, and ext4_show_quota_options prints ',jqfmt=%s' and then seq_show_option 'usrjquota' with the quota file name), so the super-options string 'rw,user_xattr,acl,jqfmt=vfsv0,usrjquota=aquota.user' has the shape and order the kernel itself emits; that kernel file is corroboration beyond the registered S077-S084 rows and is therefore not listed in 'sources'.
